vane.text: Do come in! Welcome to the Heritage Experience. Free tote bag with every signature.

rail_guard.text: Piccadilly Station. Where do you fancy going?

warden_pop.text: We are not fencing anything. We are curating access.
The tote bags are excellent, by the way. Very sturdy.

tram_fan.text: Manchester's Metrolink opened in 1992. I was there. I had a flask.
It was the first modern tram system in the country. I know because I tell everybody.

boater.text: This is the Rochdale Canal. Opened 1804, closed in the 1950s, reopened in 2002. Nine lives, like a cat.
The Bridgewater Canal, round the corner, was the first proper canal in Britain. Built in 1761 to carry coal.

student.text: Rutherford split the atom here in 1917. And the first stored-program computer ran here in 1948. They called it the Baby.
The Baby weighed about a tonne. Teething problems, you could say.

busker.text: Any requests? I know nine chords and a song about the rain.
Everyone asks for the one about the rain.

town_hall_guide.text: The Town Hall opened in 1877. Gothic revival, big clock, bigger bees.
The worker bee is Manchester's emblem. It stands for hard work. The city did not invent the bee, but it did perfect the queue.

bee_fan.text: Spot the bees on the lamp posts, the pavements, the bins. They're everywhere.
The worker bee has been the city's symbol since the Victorians. Busy city, busy bees, busy brolly.
